subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Choe <sara.choe@aurorafinance.com>, Matthew Jones <matthew.jones@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Hi Sara / Matt —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the highlights from our discovery so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed or correct details.

Summary of pain points
- Unpredictable latency and throughput on multi-tenant endpoints during daily batch jobs and morning spikes; peak latency spikes are impacting customer-facing flows.
- Cost volatility: previous providers' autoscaling behavior caused big cost spikes during testing windows.
- Data isolation & compliance: Aurora needs strict separation for sensitive financial models and audit trails.

Current stack and constraints
- Prod inference today: self-hosted on AWS EKS using mixed GPU instances + OpenAI API fallbacks for overflow.
- Traffic: ~2M inference requests/month; baseline ~8 TPS, peak ~40 TPS during batch windows and product releases.
- Typical prompt lengths: 150-400 tokens; small% of very long sequences (~>2k tokens) for remediation workflows.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS required for some models.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable p95 latency for short prompts: target <= 200ms at peak TPS
- Consistent throughput: support sustained 40 TPS with burst to 80 TPS for short windows
- Isolation & audit: dedicated GPU pools, per-tenant KV/cache isolation, and detailed audit logs for each request
- Cost predictability: monthly committed capacity with clear burst pricing to avoid surprise overages

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with per-customer isolation and SLA targets
- Autoscaling / burst policies: configurable policies allowing predictable bursts up to a configured limit, plus overflow routing to hosted API if desired
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, request traces, model-level dashboards
- Compliance: SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration, and audit log exports

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Marissa (SE) to validate latency and throughput assumptions and to size the GPU footprint — propose Wed Oct 14, 10:00 AM PT
2) Rafael to send preliminary capacity estimate & mutual action plan (attached) by Mon Oct 12
3) Aurora to share sample request distribution (token histogram & daily TPS) and any security questionnaire items today/tomorrow
4) Follow-up pricing ballpark after sizing; formal quote after deep-dive

Attachments included: aurora_capacity_estimate.xlsx (prelim), mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf, SOC2_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127
From: Matthew Jones <matthew.jones@aurorafinance.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Choe <sara.choe@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Thanks Rafael — this is great and captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 40 TPS peak is during nightly reconciliation windows (~20 mins) and again during morning settlement spikes (~10-15 mins). Sustained baseline is closer to 6-8 TPS.
- For long sequences we said ~5% of traffic, mostly for historical ledger summarization (can be queued).
- SOC2 artifacts are critical — we'll need the SOC2 Type II report and an architecture diagram showing network boundaries for dedicated pools.

We’re good for the deep-dive on Wed Oct 14 at 10:00 AM PT — Sara added it to our calendar. For the preliminary capacity estimate, could you include an option with a small reserved commit + predictable burst headroom vs. a larger reserved commit that reduces per-token cost? That will help our procurement team evaluate tradeoffs.

Also, can you send a short checklist of the data access/KMS steps required for on-boarding?

Appreciate it — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Matt
Matthew Jones
Head of Platform Engineering | Aurora Finance
matthew.jones@aurorafinance.com | +1 (617) 555-0189
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Quick notes for the deep-dive:
- I’ll prepare two sizing options (small reserved + burst headroom, and larger reserved commit).
- Please ask Aurora to bring: token histogram by endpoint, percentiles for request size, and a list of models they plan to run in Dedicated (family + quantization expectations).
- Key technical questions to validate on Wed:
  * What are their cold-start tolerances for rarely used models?
  * Do they need multi-az failover for Dedicated pools?
  * Do they require HSM-backed key management or is KMS sufficient?

I’ll bring an internal checklist for onboarding and a draft runbook for autoscaling/burst policies.
